editorial:
Ever wondered what happens when a world-famous expert is actually a total fraud? You get this hilarious ride where Liz and Jill, two college students, go on a mission to find the greatest acting teacher of the decade. They track down a guy named Kenneth LaPoubelle, who everyone treats like a god. The vibe is light and chaotic, focusing on the weird energy of a classroom where the teacher is way more confused than the students. It is a great look at how people can be fooled by a big reputation and a fancy name, making you laugh at how dysfunctional the whole group becomes.

The acting is the best part here because the actors are playing people who are bad at acting, which is a fun twist. The pacing stays quick, though some of the interview scenes drag a bit. If you love comedies that poke fun at art and ego, you will have a blast with this one.
endingExplained: At the end, the mask finally falls off Kenneth LaPoubelle. After Liz and Jill interview enough former students, they prove that Ken has no real method and just makes things up as he goes. The class ends in a huge, messy blowout where the students realize they were being tricked. Ken tries to save face, but the truth is out. Everyone walks away realizing that true talent cannot be faked by a fancy title.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mockumentaries or movies about fake experts.
